page: Microsoft Azure D48ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPSv5 family, powered by ARM architecture. The instance runs on an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. It provides 48 dedicated physical cores mapped 1:1 to 48 vCPUs with single-threaded execution per core. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache distribution includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance includes hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions, but lacks x86-specific vector extensions. It provides no local temporary storage and no onboard GPUs, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallelized compute capability, led by high multi-core stress-ng scores (85,033.61) and fast Clang software compilation throughput (40,274.0). Decompression scaling under multi-threaded bzip3 is also reliable. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,118.0 and lower single-threaded gzip compression bandwidth (22.22 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth delivers steady intermediate performance, maintaining 139.87 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB read operations and 69.35 GB/sec on large block writes.

The 48 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading eliminate hyperthreading contention, leading to consistent performance distribution across concurrent tasks. From a qualitative resource-efficiency perspective, the ARM architecture offers high core counts and large memory pools suitable for horizontally scalable microservices, static web serving (tested at 26.42 GB/sec), Redis key-value workloads (yielding over 30 million set operations per second), and continuous integration pipelines compiling software at scale.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ps_v5 is a general-purpose ARM-based virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 3.0 GHz and 192.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, providing 4.0 GB per core without simultaneous multithreading. It includes no bundled local disk storage and no GPU acceleration, depending entirely on network storage volumes. Benchmark data indicates solid multi-threaded performance, demonstrating high throughput during parallel compilation tasks and multi-core CPU stress tests. In contrast, per-thread single-core metrics and sequential decompression bandwidth are comparatively modest. Memory subsystem throughput remains consistent across read and write operations. The D48ps_v5 is suited for parallelized enterprise workloads, multi-threaded backend services, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, and high-throughput CI/CD build environments running on 64-bit ARM platforms.
